title: APTQ: Attention-aware Post-Training Mixed-Precision Quantization for Large Language Models
problem: Large Language Models require high computational resources and substantial memory, making deployment on edge devices challenging. Mixed-precision quantization must reduce model size while preserving inference accuracy.
motivation: Efficient LLM deployment on edge devices is critical for enabling practical applications in resource-constrained environments.
method: APTQ applies mixed-precision quantization by selecting per-layer precision levels based on Hessian trace sensitivity metrics. It uniquely incorporates both second-order weight information via Hessian matrices and the nonlinear effects of attention outputs on model predictions, enabling precision reduction decisions that maintain performance.
key_novelty: First consideration of nonlinear effects of attention outputs in conjunction with Hessian-based sensitivity metrics for mixed-precision LLM quantization.
contributions: Attention-aware framework for mixed-precision quantization incorporating attention output effects
Hessian trace-based sensitivity metric for informed precision selection across layers
Achieves 4-bit average quantization with near full-precision performance (5.22 perplexity on C4)
State-of-the-art zero-shot results: 68.24% (LLaMa-7B) and 70.48% (LLaMa-13B) at 3.8-bit average bitwidth
limitations: Paper does not discuss specific limitations or failure cases.
primary_theme: Attention-aware mixed-precision quantization for LLM edge deployment
